title: Finite-projective quotient Hom evaluation before cohomology
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative coefficient ring, J an ideal and U a coefficient-sized pro-etale site object. Let P,Q be integer cochain complexes of A-modules, with P bounded between a and b and every P^i finite projective; Q is arbitrary. Form their actual ordinary quotient models C_n(P), C_n(Q) using [def-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-model-complexes]. Write G for the additive group of sections of a constant A-module sheaf at the slice terminal object, as in [def-sfb-adic-short-complex-quotient-tower]. Let K=moduleHomComplex(P,Q) from [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. There exist chain isomorphisms from the ordinary global abelian-group Hom complex HomComplex(C_n(P),C_n(Q)) to the termwise G-realization of K/J^(n+1)K. In every cochain degree q these isomorphisms intertwine the actual successor scalar change, conjugated by the ordinary balancing isomorphisms, with G applied to the canonical algebraic quotient transition. This is a chain-level evaluation assertion: it assumes neither weak contractibility nor any exactness of general sheaf sections, and asserts nothing about homotopy classes or cohomology.

source.place: Tag 09C6, the displayed quotient total-Hom calculation; Modules on Sites Tag 093T; More on Algebra Tag 0A8H.

proof.text: Use the additive single-module quotient Hom comparison. Its comparison on arbitrary modules is natural for precomposition and postcomposition, bijective for a finite projective source, and commutes with the ordinary successor balancing maps.

Project a module Hom cochain onto each component and apply the single-module comparison. Two-variable naturality identifies the two summands of the signed Hom differential separately, giving a chain map from the realized algebraic quotient Hom complex to the ordinary sheaf Hom complex.

Only source degrees in the finite interval [a,b] survive. The sum of component projections followed by single-cochain inclusions is the identity, including when the interval is empty. Additivity preserves this finite identity. The component comparisons are bijective, so the chain map is degreewise bijective and hence an isomorphism.

Naturality of the actual quotient transition with respect to each component projection and the module successor identity give the square on all cochains. Apply the inverse of the chain isomorphism to obtain the displayed successor equation for e.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09C6, quotient total-Hom calculation; finite component assembly written in Lean by Y5.

mathlib_searches.query: Evaluation of Hom cochains between bounded finite projective constant quotient complexes is a natural isomorphism with sections of the quotient of the algebraic Hom complex
mathlib_searches.results: msearch.py returned HomComplex.Cochain.mk, shiftEval, Cochain.fromSingleEquiv, Cochain.toSingleEquiv and HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoApp. These supply cochain and component APIs but no quotient/constant evaluation comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: Homotopy classes of maps between constant finite projective complexes are sections of algebraic Hom complex cohomology, commuting with quotient scalars
mathlib_searches.results: HomComplex.CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv and toHom_mk identify ordinary cohomology classes with homotopy classes. They do not identify the underlying quotient sheaf Hom cochains with constant algebraic Hom cochains.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Generic descent API only, no chain evaluation comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: HomComplex constant quotient sections; cochain equiv; scalarChangeCompTo; SiteConstantModuleHom; search Mathlib/Algebra/Homology and both library roots
mathlib_searches.results: SiteConstantModuleHom gives the finite-presentation internal-Hom comparison; AdicResiduePerfectReductionComparison and private AdicPerfectModel helpers give scalar balancing and constant scalar extension. Neither compares arbitrary global Hom cochains or supplies the successor equation in all degrees. ScalarPerfectDualRealization treats Hom into the unit complex only. Blueprint search Hom complex found three unrelated nodes.

lean.statement:
theorem adicPerfectHomCochains (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ℤ)
    (a b : ℤ) (_ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (_hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (_hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X i)) :
    let G := AdicCohomology.sections
      ((coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X).over U) (Over.mk (𝟙 U)) ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat A) AddCommGrpCat
    let K := CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex P Q
    let C := fun n : ℕ ↦ CochainComplex.HomComplex
      (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U P n)
      (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U Q n)
    let D := fun n : ℕ ↦ (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
      (((AdicCohomology.quotient J (n + 1)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ, C n ≅ D n,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ)
        (z : Cochain (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U P (n + 1))
          (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U Q (n + 1)) q),
        (e n).hom.f q
          (((Cochain.ofHom (adicPerfectQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U P n).inv).comp
            (z.map (change (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep.{u, v} X J U n)))
              (zero_add q)).comp
                (Cochain.ofHom (adicPerfectQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U Q n).hom)
                  (add_zero q)) =
          G.map ((AdicCohomology.transition J
            (Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.le_succ n) 1)).app (K.X q))
              ((e (n + 1)).hom.f q z)
